people.name: Jesus
aliases: Jesus the son of Sirach Eleazar
people.description: Author of the book, a teacher of wisdom from Jerusalem.
people.identity_note: WEB 50:27 reads 'I Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar, of Jerusalem'. Parent link to Sirach is from this verse; how Eleazar fits (Sirach's own second name, Sirach's father, or an ancestor) is unclear in the Greek. The Hebrew (MS B) gives a longer chain (Simeon son of Jeshua son of Eleazar ben Sira). The first-person speaker of ch. 51 is presumably the same man but is not named there. The grandson-translator and the 'grandfather' wording come from the Greek prologue, which is absent from this WEB VPL file.

people.name: Sirach
people.description: Father (or family name) of Jesus, the author of the book.
people.identity_note: 'Sirach' may be a family name rather than the literal father; kept as the stated parent per 50:27. Not linked to Eleazar because the relation is not stated unambiguously.

people.name: Eleazar
people.description: Name attached to Sirach in the author's self-designation; exact relationship unclear.
people.identity_note: Greek 'son of Sirach Eleazar' is ambiguous: Eleazar may be Sirach's father (task brief reads 'son of Sirach son of Eleazar'), an ancestor, or a second name of Sirach. No parent link asserted; reviewer may merge as an alias of Sirach or link as Sirach's father.

people.name: Simon
people.description: High priest, son of Onias, praised for repairing and fortifying the temple and city (usually identified as Simon II).
people.identity_note: Usually identified as Simon II (high priest c. 219-196 BC); not an existing entity.

people.name: Onias
people.description: Father of Simon the high priest.
people.identity_note: Usually identified as Onias II; may need merging with an Onias entry from the Maccabees census if one is created (the Onias of 1MA 12 / 2MA 3-4 are other individuals).

people.name: Enoch
people.description: Pleased the Lord and was taken up.
people.identity_note: Taken-up Enoch = son of Jared (Gen 5), not Cain's son.

people.name: Noah
people.description: Found righteous; preserved a remnant through the flood.

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Father of a multitude of nations, kept the covenant.

people.name: Isaac
people.description: Received the covenant assurance for Abraham's sake.

people.name: Jacob
people.description: Received the blessing; his portions divided among twelve tribes.
people.identity_note: Other 'Jacob' and all 'Israel' occurrences (23:12, 24:8, 24:23, 36:11, 45:5, 45:17, 46:14, 47:22, 48:10, 49:10; 17:17, 36:12, 37:25 etc.) denote the people and are not counted.

people.name: Moses
people.description: Man loved by God and men who received the law face to face.

people.name: Aaron
people.description: Brother of Moses of the tribe of Levi, given the everlasting priesthood.
people.identity_note: Aaron is Moses' brother (45:6). 36:17 ('blessing of Aaron'), 50:13 and 50:16 ('sons of Aaron') name him as ancestor of the priesthood.

people.name: Dathan
people.description: Conspired against Aaron in the wilderness.

people.name: Abiram
people.description: Conspired with Dathan against Aaron in the wilderness.

people.name: Korah
people.description: Leader of the congregation that rose against Aaron.

people.name: Phinehas
people.description: Zealous priest, third in glory, given a covenant of peace.

people.name: Eleazar (son of Aaron)
people.description: Father of Phinehas.
people.identity_note: Text says only 'Phinehas the son of Eleazar'; this is Aaron's son. WEB name form is 'Eleazar'; suffix added to distinguish from eleazar-sirach.

people.name: Joshua
people.description: Son of Nun, successor of Moses, valiant in war.

people.name: Nun
people.description: Father of Joshua.

people.name: Caleb
people.description: Son of Jephunneh who with Joshua withstood the people and entered the hill country.

people.name: Jephunneh
people.description: Father of Caleb.

people.name: Samuel
people.description: Prophet of the Lord who established a kingdom, judged, and prophesied after death.

people.name: the king (Saul)
people.description: King anointed by Samuel, to whom Samuel showed his end after death.
people.identity_note: Not named; 'his anointed' (46:19) and 'the king' to whom Samuel prophesied after death (46:20, cf. 1 Sam 28) can only be Saul.

people.name: Nathan
people.description: Prophet in the days of David.

people.name: David
people.description: Son of Jesse, king who killed Goliath and set singers before the altar.

people.name: Jesse
people.description: Father of David.

people.name: Goliath
people.description: Boasting giant killed by David with a sling stone.

people.name: Solomon
people.description: Wise son of David who reigned in peace and built the sanctuary but bowed to women.
people.identity_note: 47:12 'After him a wise son rose up' (David's son), named in 47:13.

people.name: Rehoboam
people.description: Solomon's offspring whose counsel made the people revolt.

people.name: Jeroboam
people.description: Son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
people.identity_note: Son of Nebat = first king of the northern kingdom, not Jeroboam II.

people.name: Nebat
people.description: Father of Jeroboam.

people.name: Elijah
people.description: Fiery prophet who shut the heavens and was taken up in a whirlwind.

people.name: Elisha
people.description: Filled with Elijah's spirit; his body prophesied after burial.
people.identity_note: 48:8 'prophets to succeed after you' alludes to Elisha's anointing but is plural; not counted as a ref.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.description: King who fortified Jerusalem and dug a water tunnel; did what pleased the Lord.
people.descent_note: 48:22 calls David 'his ancestor'; distant ancestor, not a parent.
people.identity_note: 48:23 'the king' whose life was prolonged = Hezekiah.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.description: Assyrian king who invaded in Hezekiah's days.

people.name: Rabshakeh
people.description: Envoy sent by Sennacherib against Zion.
people.identity_note: Rabshakeh is a title in Kings/Isaiah; the existing entity treats it as a person, so mapped.

people.name: Isaiah
people.description: Prophet through whom Jerusalem was delivered and who foresaw the end of time.

people.name: Josiah
people.description: Reforming king whose memory is sweet.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.description: Prophet sanctified in the womb, mistreated by the kings.

people.name: Ezekiel
people.description: Saw the vision of glory on the chariot of the cherubim.

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.description: Post-exilic leader likened to a signet ring.

people.name: Jesus
people.description: Son of Josedek, who with Zerubbabel built the house.
people.identity_note: Greek 'Jesus son of Josedek' = Joshua/Jeshua son of Jehozadak the post-exilic high priest (Hag 1:1, Ezra 3:2). joshua-ezr2 ('High priest during the rebuilding') chosen; jeshua-ezr2 (Levite) and jeshua-neh3 are different people. Two entries named 'Jesus' in this file: use existing_id to disambiguate.

people.name: Josedek
people.description: Father of Jesus (Joshua) the high priest.
people.identity_note: Mapped to jehozadak (father of Joshua the high priest), not jozadak (Ezra 10 entry).

people.name: Nehemiah
people.description: Raised up the fallen walls and gates of Jerusalem.

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Leader of his kindred whose bones were cared for.

people.name: Shem
people.description: Honored among men.

people.name: Seth
people.description: Honored among men.

people.name: Adam
people.description: First man, created from dust, above every living thing.

people.name: Lot
people.description: Abraham's nephew, whose neighbors (Sodom) the Lord did not spare.

excluded_names.Israel: people/nation (no verse refers to the patriarch as an individual)

notes: No prologue in this WEB VPL file: SIR begins at 1:1 and there is no 0:x or 'Prologue' line (none in the .xml/.sql either; 'grandfather' does not occur). The translator's prologue (grandson of Jesus, who came to Egypt in the 38th year of Euergetes) therefore cannot be cited, so the unnamed grandson-translator is NOT entered as a person; add him only if a source text with the prologue is used. 'The judges, every one by his name' (46:11) and 'the twelve prophets' (49:10) are collective references, recorded here only as notes, not as people. Job: the WEB (Greek) 49:9 reads 'he remembered the enemies in rainstorm' with no mention of Job (the Hebrew mentions Job), so Job is not included. No Ptolemy appears in the WEB text of SIR. Unnamed allusions not entered: 25:24 'the beginning of sin came from a woman' (Eve, but generic); 48:5 the dead man raised by Elijah (widow's son); 48:6 and 48:8 plural kings/prophets; 16:7 giants; 16:10 600,000 footmen; 50:13,16 sons of Aaron (collective). Two entries have WEB name 'Jesus' (author 50:27 and son of Josedek 49:12); disambiguated by new_id/existing_id. 'Eleazar (son of Aaron)' carries a parenthetical to separate it from eleazar-sirach. Refs for Moses, Aaron, Joshua, Samuel, David, Solomon, Elijah and Simon include contiguous verses of their eulogies where they are the clear subject by pronoun.
